data.name: Chidaatma
data.gender_notes: Chidaatma is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Chidaatma is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Chid' meaning consciousness and 'Atma' meaning soul. It represents the supreme consciousness that pervades all beings and is the inner self or soul of every individual. The name Chidaatma carries the meaning “Lord of Consciousness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chidaatma usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of consciousness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chidaatma belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Consciousness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chidaatma total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chidaatma holds a deep cultural significance for Hindus, as it is derived from the ancient Sanskrit language. The use of Sanskrit names has been a tradition in Hinduism for centuries, reflecting the rich heritage and spiritual roots of the culture. The name Chidaatma reminds us of our connection to the universe and the divine consciousness that lies within each of us.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Chidaatma lies in its emphasis on the soul or atma as being a manifestation of the supreme consciousness or Chid. It reminds us of our innate connection to the divine and encourages us to continue our spiritual journey inwards, towards self-realization and union with the ultimate truth. The name serves as a constant reminder of the importance of maintaining a conscious awareness of our inner selves and the divine presence within us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chidaatma signifies the innermost Self, the Atman, which is pure, eternal, and infinitely conscious. The name suggests the quest for realizing one's true nature beyond the physical body and transient experiences.

historical_references.reference: Chidaatma is a form of Vishnu, revered primarily in the states of Rajasthan and Gujarat in India. It is believed that Chidaatma appeared before Raja Chidhar of Jodhpur when he was on a hunting expedition. The king was filled with remorse after accidentally killing a Jain monk on his lands. Chidaatma is said to have appeared before him and forgave him for his mistake, asking him to build a temple in his name.
historical_references.context: Hunting expedition by Raja Chidhar of Jodhpur leads to encounter with Chidaatma, a form of Vishnu

historical_references.reference: Another legend associated with Chidaatma is that of the Rajput king Rao Jaswant Singh of Jodhpur. It is believed that during a battle, Rao Jaswant Singh's army was losing ground against the enemy. In desperation, the king called upon Chidaatma for help. The deity is said to have appeared before the army, instilling courage and strength in the soldiers, leading to a victory for Jodhpur.
